note: Rebuild of the item text withdrawn under irw#1594 (item-to-text mapping unverifiable). Sheet1's STOP (links populated) was overridden: those links are the withdrawn, mismapped curation, not in-flight work; drop this CSV if the STOP should hold. CODE DERIVATION: script-generated integer -- data/political_psychology.R assigns row_number() over unique(item) after pivoting yllanon.csv, i.e. column order after dropping 12 non-item columns. Re-ran that logic over the raw OSF file (osf.io/3pwvb 'Data and Codebook/yllanon.csv', sha256 prefix 7e82c8f3c72c6cce): crosswalk 1=def,2=crime,3=terror,4=poor,5=health,6=econ,7=abort,8=unemploy,9=blkaid,10=adopt,11=imm,12=vaccines,13=guns,14=djt,15=interest,16-20=friends_1..5,21=tense,22=death,23=ewry,24=values,25=ideo,26=partyid,27=votereport,28=voting,29=climate,30-32=beh_att_1..3,33=beh_identity,34=virusthreat,35=quarantine,36=sickleave,37=fourth. Per-item n and mean identical to irw_fetch for 36/37 items, all 245 live item x resp cells identical. This confirms #1594's suspicion that the withdrawn curation was misaligned (it put friends_1 text on item 27, which is votereport). TEXT: variable-name -> wording from the study's own Qualtrics exports (OSF 'Materials - Qualtrics Format', DataExportTag = the data file's column name; wave 26 .qsf sha256 prefix b6ec66b31eca0781, wave 1_Clinton for votereport, wave 9 for fourth, trashed questions excluded -- the .qsf trash holds 5-point ideo/partyid variants that were never fielded; the Word exports show only the 7-point versions). Cross-checked against codebook1.html's per-variable descriptions and value labels (friends_1..5 = Liberals, Conservatives, Moderates, Republicans, Democrats; beh_att_1..3 = poor, economy, healthcare), which agree with the .qsf choice IDs. Whitespace/HTML ( , line breaks) normalised; wording otherwise verbatim incl. leading '1. ' numbering on abort and beh_identity options and the leading ellipsis on beh_att sub-items. friends and beh_att are Qualtrics matrix questions: stem in section_prompt (sections _2, _3), row label in item_text. OPTIONS: Qualtrics anchor labels carry the displayed scale-point digit glued on ('Greatly decrease defense spending1'); the digit was stripped (the codebook prints the same labels without it). Unlabelled intermediate points (displayed as bare '2'..'6') are left blank rather than padded. Don't know / haven't-thought codes are NA in the live table and get no rows. DEVIATIONS: item 27 votereport resp 3 is the script's merge of source codes 4 'I did not vote' and 5 'I planned to vote, but I forgot' (source 3 'A different candidate' and 6 'I do not remember' are NA), shipped as 'I did not vote / I planned to vote, but I forgot'. Item 28 voting is not a survey question: it is 2016 vote choice from Prolific's records (codebook), script-coded trump=1, clinton=2, other=3; item_text is the codebook's description (trailing parenthetical about missingness dropped) and option_text the data file's own strings. DATA NOTE: the live table drops beh_identity (item 33) code 8 'I would vote for another party, namely:' (35 rows) although the committed data/political_psychology.R only NAs code 9 -- the live table was built from a version of the script that also NA'd 8; not a defect in the shipped text, but the committed script does not reproduce the live table exactly. The committed script also has a syntax error (a line beginning with |> after a blank line) and would not run as written. RIGHTS: ANES-derived items (spending, abortion, ideology, party ID, etc.) -- instrument_rights_register ANES/NES verdict ship (applied, not re-derived); remaining items are the authors' own, OSF project licence CC-By Attribution 4.0 International (api.osf.io node 3pwvb), no restriction located.
public_note: Item 27 (2016 vote report) stores a merged category 3 = 'did not vote' or 'planned to vote but forgot' (voters for other candidates are missing), and item 28 is not a survey question but the respondent's 2016 vote recorded by Prolific.

source_ref: Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/MTQGSF (CC0 1.0): 'SUPPLEMENTARY ONLINE APPENDIX_FULL FINANCIAL LITERACY TESTS.docx' (datafile 10809639, md5 bd1ec999c82aadc71bbd1e7fbacb46f4), Table 1 'Original Polish version' (item_text, correct_response from bold runs) and Table 2 'English version translated from the original Polish version' (item_text_translated); for_replication.tab original Stata file (datafile 10629129, md5 c9579643b1333b65f6f1d881bb57653a) value labels for option_text. Paper: Cwynar, Bialowolski, Weziak-Bialowolska & Porzak (2025), Int J Consumer Studies 49(4), doi:10.1111/ijcs.70083 -- closed access, 403 on Wiley full/pdfdirect and WebFetch, not read.
note: MAPPING: code derivation pattern 1 (data/bialowolski_2024_financial_literacy.py keeps the Stata column names FL_1..FL_17, FL_19), but the Stata variable labels read only 'Poprawnosc odpowiedzi : FL_n' (correctness of answer) and carry no wording, so the FL->question tie is NOT data_labels. The appendix numbers its questions Q1..Q18 while the deposit has FL_1..FL_19 with FL_18 absent; shipped FL_n=Qn for n=1..17 and FL_19=Q18 (paper_order). This assumes the FL_18 gap is a question dropped from both appendix and data, not a renumbering; the closed paper was not reachable to confirm. Step 5b route 8 + content-pair structure is PARTIAL (see verification row). DESIGN: respondents were randomly assigned one of three wordings (feminized / masculinized / gender-neutral; deposit columns sex{m,f}ver{m,f,u}, not in the IRW table), and option wording also differs by version for Q2, Q3, Q5, Q6, Q10, Q12. item_text therefore carries all three versions, each prefixed with the appendix's own column header ('Wersja sfeminizowana: ... | Wersja zmaskulinizowana: ... | Wersja neutralna: ...'), and each version is its cell's paragraphs (stem then answer choices) joined with ' / ' -- a formatting change, words otherwise verbatim incl. the source's doubled spaces. For Q13/Q14 the appendix cell prints 'Pytanie otwarte - podana odpowiedz. Prawidlowa to 0 zl.' (open question; the answer key) in the option position; transcribed as printed, so those items' item_text contains the key. correct_response = the bold text in the Polish appendix table (key_source: source_published); a single string when identical across versions, else the same three-version labelled form. Q4 neutral version bolds 'Akcjach.' for 'Najwiecej zalezy od Ciebie' (English 'The least depends on you') -- transcribed as the source bolds it, not adjudicated. RESP: resp is 0/1 correctness. option_text = the Stata value labels 'Odpowiedz niepoprawna'(0)/'Odpowiedz poprawna'(1); option_text_translated 'Incorrect answer'/'Correct answer' is this project's translation (hence translation_source=mixed: item/instruction English is the study's own appendix translation, option English is machine_translation-class, two short scoring labels). Value labels also define 9='Nie wiem' and, on FL_14 only, 2='Odpowiedz zblizona do poprawnej' (close to correct), but neither code occurs in the deposited data (only 0/1, no missing, 4389 x 18) -- don't-know was evidently folded into 0 before deposit, which the study's scoring implies but the deposit does not state. Live per-item proportions equal the deposit's to 3 dp (e.g. FL_2 .166, FL_16 .958). LANGUAGE: administered in Polish; the appendix notes its English 'is translated from the original Polish version' and that nuances may be lost. RIGHTS: study's own questions (adapted from the well-known Lusardi-Mitchell-type financial literacy set per the abstract), published in the study's CC0 deposit; no fee/permission/NC/ND/redistribution clause located; no register row applies; shipped on silence. No register row written.
public_note: Respondents were randomly assigned one of three wordings of each question (feminized, masculinized, gender-neutral Polish), so item_text lists all three; resp is scored 0/1, with 'don't know' counted as incorrect, and the tie of item code FL_19 to the appendix's 18th question is inferred from order (the deposit has no FL_18).
